newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yarn spinner optimism rules Bremen cotton market.
newsitem.headline: Yarn spinner optimism rules Bremen cotton market.

text.p: Increased capacity utilisation at European spinning mills boosted sentiment among raw cotton buyers, a market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
Yarn and fabric prices were seen rising on demand from domestic and overseas and this underpinned cotton demand.
The textile industry had completed maintenance shut-downs and administrative breaks over the Christmas and new year period.
Its customers were seeking a broad range of cotton qualities for delivery in the first half of 1997.
An industrial fair in Frankfurt displaying latest trend in home furnishings was expected to contribute to higher ordering activity.
Bremen cotton stocks rose by 3,316 bales in the fortnight ended Jan 10 to 31,603 bales compared with 53,554 bales recorded a year ago.
The Exchange reported upland cotton trades in Central Asian standards 3 and 4, as well as Westafrican, Syrian, Israeli and Zimbabwean origins for 1997 dates.
El Paso-Acala, California SJV and Mexico-Juarez traded for the current quarter.
